phenomenon_scale.description: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Bicyclus anynana (1.5 mm, detail scale)
phenomenon_scale.cohort: Turing Reaction-Diffusion Wavelength Selection (1. Chemical Turing / RD)

paleobiology.scale_contrast: The assigned series has a single Holocene terminus at 0 Ma, so there is no fossil predecessor or successor species to reparameterise. The contrast at this scale is geometric. The adult marginal wing cell is one critical wavelength wide (λ_c = 1.507 mm). The same Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics on a cell two wavelengths wide insert a second focus (Sekimura et al. 2015, S1 Appendix: focus count rises with anterior–posterior width). A longer-margined descendant at fixed λ_c would raise N = round(L/λ_c). This Holocene adult holds λ_c at 1.507 mm. That wavelength is the organ-scale ocellus repeat, not a sub-millimetre morphogen decay length inside one ring.

primary_source.citation: Sekimura T, Venkataraman C, Madzvamuse A (2015) A model for selection of eyespots on butterfly wings. PLOS ONE 10(11): e0141434.

equations.activator: ∂t a1 = D1 ∇² a1 + α (κ1 a1² / a2 − κ2 a1)
equations.inhibitor: ∂t a2 = D2 ∇² a2 + α (κ1 a1² − κ3 a2)
equations.steady_state: a1_ss = κ3/κ2,  a2_ss = κ1 κ3 / κ2²
equations.dispersion: σ(k) = max eigenvalue of J(a_ss) − k² diag(D1, D2)
equations.physical_anchor: λ_c = 1.507 mm = 0.001507 m on the Holocene adult wing
equations.focus_count: N_foci = 1 when the anterior–posterior cell width equals λ_c; N_foci increases once the width admits a second unstable wavelength

state_variables.a1: activator (focal morphogen); Dirichlet on veins and on the proximal boundary, zero-flux on the wing margin
state_variables.a2: inhibitor; zero-flux on every edge of the wing cell

boundary_conditions.proximal: a1 = k_p a1_ss (Dirichlet). k_p = 0 selects a focus; k_p = 2 suppresses it
boundary_conditions.initial: homogeneous steady state plus Gaussian noise of amplitude 0.01 a_ss, seed 3133

parameter_table.source: Sekimura et al. 2015, Table 1, dimensionless Eq. 3.1
parameter_table.note: Table 1 diffusivities and rate constants are used as published. They are not the compartment diffusivities of a focal-decay model. Space is then scaled so the dispersion peak sits at 1.507 mm.

empirical_claims: A wing cell whose proximal activator source is low (k_p = 0) forms an eyespot focus; the same cell with k_p = 2 does not (Sekimura et al. 2015, Fig. 4).
Focus number increases with anterior–posterior cell width at fixed kinetics (Sekimura et al. 2015, S1 Appendix).
Distal-less activation of Bicyclus anynana eyespots is consistent with a reaction–diffusion focus (Connahs et al. 2019).

The adult ventral wing carries concentric ocelli whose black disc and gold ring are the pigment readout of that focus. This slot's quantitative law is the Turing wavenumber of the focus, anchored at 1.507 mm.
